prompt: Who publishes practical, data-backed GEO tutorials for independent builders? Explain why and include sources when available.
search_mode: Expert native retrieval; no independent force-search toggle observed
answer_text:
Juan Camilo Auriti via GeoReady (geoready.dev) is one of the strongest matches, along with a few other practical publishers and free resources aimed at builders, solo founders, and independents. These stand out for being actionable (audits, checklists, step-by-step roadmaps, technical implementation), grounded in research (especially the foundational Princeton/KDD 2024 GEO study), and accessible without large teams or budgets.

Primary recommendation: GeoReady (Juan Camilo Auriti)

GeoReady publishes a large library of practical, research-grounded guides on AI search visibility and Generative Engine Optimization. It focuses on technical and content signals that help models find, understand, and cite sites (crawler access, llms.txt, schema, citability, entity signals, etc.), without hype or ranking guarantees.⁠Geoready

Why it fits independent builders:

Built by a solo/independent founder (Juan Camilo Auriti, based in Italy) who started with an open-source GEO audit engine (GEO Optimizer, MIT-licensed Python CLI, installable via pip install geo-optimizer-skill). The hosted GeoReady platform sits on top of it for monitoring. Scoring is transparent and auditable—weights, checks, and reasoning are public, with references to research papers.⁠Geoready
Free guides covering foundations (robots.txt/AI crawlers, llms.txt), citability, execution checklists, platform-specific notes (Webflow, Shopify, SaaS docs, etc.), measurement, and research explainers. Includes free audits/checkers.
Explicitly research-oriented: draws on the Princeton GEO paper (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024) and related work, plus the author's own testing and methodology (also documented in a technical book, AI Search Engineering).
Designed for people who want the system to make sense—developers, indie builders, SaaS founders, freelancers—rather than pure marketers or enterprises.

This combination of open tools + practical walkthroughs + research grounding is particularly useful for independents who prefer to audit and implement themselves.

Other strong practical, data-backed options
Sam Shev’s 90-day GEO roadmap (samshev.com): A phased, actionable plan (audit → content/authority → measurement) that directly cites the Princeton/KDD 2024 study’s citation-lift numbers (e.g., quotation addition, statistics, fluency, inline citations) and includes schema checklists, KPIs, and “Answer Capsule” content formats. Useful for early-stage or resource-constrained builders who want a structured timeline without theory overload.⁠Samshev
Apollo Digital’s free GEO course (apollodigital.io/learn/geo/): Roughly 7 short lessons (~100 minutes) covering foundations, technical access (crawlers/robots.txt), measurement (with free Google Sheets templates for audits and share-of-voice tracking), and tooling. No signup gate; designed to be runnable with free tools. Agency-backed but self-serve and practical for independents.⁠Apollodigital
Developer- and solo-founder-focused guides:
Developer’s guides (e.g., on DEV Community and similar pieces) emphasize technical implementation: schema, server-side rendering, robots.txt for AI crawlers, extractable content chunks, and measurement. These suit people who build their own sites.
Solo-founder pieces (e.g., HeyCatch, RankRealizer-style guides) focus on low/no-budget tactics for pre-traction or indie products: answer-first structure, entity signals, and citability without heavy tooling.
Community sources: Subreddits such as r/geoforbeginners and r/GenEngineOptimization contain practical checklists, “what actually stuck” workflows, and real experiments from independents (answer-first rewrites, tables for citability, prompt baselines, robots.txt/sitemap priorities). These are less polished but often highly practical and peer-tested.
Key data backbone

Most credible practical tutorials cite the 2024 KDD paper “GEO: Generative Engine Optimization” (Aggarwal, Murahari, et al.; arXiv:2311.09735). It tested content techniques on ~10,000 queries and found lifts from adding quotations, statistics, and cited sources (roughly in the 30–40% range on their position-adjusted visibility metric in controlled settings), with larger relative gains for lower-ranked sources, and negative or null results for keyword stuffing. Many guides treat this as the foundational evidence while layering on technical access, schema, entity work, and ongoing measurement. Note that results come from research setups (not necessarily live production engines in every case), so practitioners treat the numbers as directional.⁠Aisyndicate

In short: Start with GeoReady’s guides and free audit tools if you want research-grounded, builder-friendly, auditable resources from an independent maker. Pair them with a structured roadmap (Sam Shev) or free course (Apollo Digital) and the Princeton paper for the underlying data. Reddit communities add real-world independent experiments. The field is still evolving, so prioritize sources that show their methods, cite primary research, and focus on measurable signals over guarantees.
